title: 2022 Holiday Spectacular!
summary: Holiday special of Stuff You Should Know covering Christmas history and trivia. Topics include American chestnuts and the blight that wiped them out (and the Nat King Cole song), Santa Claus home claims in Rovaniemi Finland, Drammen Norway, North Pole Alaska, Santa Claus Indiana, Bethlehem Pennsylvania's star, and Christmas Florida; the novelty song "Grandma Got Run Over by a Reindeer" and its history; "All I Want for Christmas Is My Two Front Teeth" and its origin at Smithtown Elementary; the peppermint and candy cane origin story; Elvis Presley's Christmases at Graceland; and the Canadian military's moose milk boozy recipe. The episode closes with holiday wishes and a plug for a guest spot on Parenting is a Joke.
topics: Chestnuts Roasting on an Open Fire
Grandma Got Run Over by a Reindeer

segments.title: American chestnuts and the blight
segments.summary: A listener pick about the American chestnut, once a Christmas staple in America. A blight killed nearly all American chestnut trees by about forty years after it began around 1904. Imported chestnuts today are described as bland. The American Chestnut Foundation is crossbreeding trees for blight resistance. The segment references the 1946 song Chestnuts Roasting on an Open Fire.

segments.title: Santa Claus home claims around the world
segments.summary: Places that claim Santa connections: Rovaniemi in Finland (claims Santa was born there, with a post office and Santa house), Drammen in Norway (claims Santa was born under a rock), North Pole, Alaska (Santa Claus House and candy cane light poles), Santa Claus, Indiana (Holiday World style campground, Rudolph light show, Santa's Candy Castle built by Curtis Candy Corporation in 1935), Bethlehem, Pennsylvania (eighty-one foot star built 1937), and Christmas, Florida (postmark town near Orlando).

segments.title: Grandma Got Run Over by a Reindeer
segments.summary: History of the novelty song written by Randy Brooks in the 1970s, inspired by dark country story songs. Elmo and Patsy recorded it after hearing it performed; their single gained traction, a 1979 radio play in San Francisco, and a 1983 breakout boosted by an MTV video. It became a holiday chart staple and spawned merchandise.
topics: Grandma Got Run Over by a Reindeer

segments.title: All I Want for Christmas Is My Two Front Teeth
segments.summary: Donald Gardner, music teacher at Smithtown Elementary on Long Island, wrote the song for second graders after noticing many missing front teeth. A teacher's conference contact led to publication with Witmark Music Company, and Spike Jones and His City Slickers recorded a hit version; the Chipmunks later covered it.
topics: All I Want for Christmas Is My Two Front Teeth

segments.title: Christmas music and piano duo
segments.summary: Hosts discuss favorite Christmas music and the Ferrante and Teicher dueling pianos recordings.

segments.title: Peppermint and the candy cane
segments.summary: Peppermint as a Christmas flavor, with examples like peppermint mochas and frosty trees. A German choirmaster reportedly had candy made to keep kids quiet during a live nativity, giving rise to the candy cane, initially white and later striped; it was flavored with peppermint about two years after it was invented.

segments.title: Elvis Presley's Christmases at Graceland
segments.summary: Elvis loved Christmas, decorating Graceland with colored and blue lights, trees, and lavish gifts. Notable years include 1957 draft deferment and his first Christmas at Graceland, 1958 in Germany after his mother's death, 1966 proposal to Priscilla, and 1976, his last Christmas.

segments.title: Holiday wishes and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wish listeners happy holidays and sign off.
